message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). | Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. The winner of the round gets points equal to the total value of all cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each + 8 Wild cards. | 4×0, 2×1–9, 2×Skip, 2×Reverse, 2×Draw Two per color, 4×Wild, 4×Wild Draw Four. | | **Setup** | 2–10 players. | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a Wild Draw Four, the next player draws four and loses a turn). | --- ### 1. Turn Order | Action | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Play a card** | On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard card. | | **Draw a card** | If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Uno** | When you have only one card left, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. | | **Turn ends** | After playing a card (or drawing if you can’t play), the turn passes to the next player in the current direction (clockwise unless a Reverse card changes it). | --- ### 2. Card Types & Effects | Card | Effect | |------|--------| | **Number cards (0–9)** | Play normally; no special effect. | | **Skip** | The next player loses their turn. | | **Reverse** | Reverses the direction of play. In a 2‑player game, a Reverse acts like a Skip. | | **Draw Two** | The next player draws two cards and loses their turn. | | **Wild** | You choose the new color to play. | | **Wild Draw Four** | You choose the new color; the next player draws four cards and loses their turn. **(Can only be played if you have no matching color cards; otherwise you risk a challenge.)** | --- ### 3. Winning a Round | Condition | Result | |-----------|--------| | A player discards their last card | That player wins the round. | | All other players have at least one card | The winner scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Card values** | Number cards = face value; Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points; Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | --- ### 4. Winning the Game | Rule | Explanation | |------|-------------| | **Standard** | First player to reach 500 points wins. | | **House variations** | • Set a different target (e.g., 300, 1000).
• Play a single round and keep the winner.
• Keep track of points over multiple rounds. | --- ### 5. Common House Rules (Optional) | Rule | Effect | |------|--------| | **Draw 4 Challenge** | If a player suspects a Draw Four was played illegally, they can challenge. If the challenger is right, the player who played the Draw Four must draw 4 cards instead. If wrong, the challenger draws 6 cards. | | **Stacking** | Some groups allow stacking of Draw Two or Draw Four cards (e.g., if you’re faced with a Draw Two, you can play another Draw Two to pass the penalty). | | **No “Uno” shout** | Some play without shouting “UNO”; instead, the next player must call it out. | | **Multiple decks** | For larger groups, combine two Uno decks. | --- ### 6. Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on cards, try to keep a variety of colors so you can always play something. 2. **Save Wilds** – Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. 3. **Watch opponents** – If someone is close to Uno, be ready to play a Skip or Draw Two to stop them. 4. **Mind the direction** – A Reverse can be a powerful defensive move, especially in a 2‑player game. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
